subject: Biotechnology
title: Antibody-Drug Conjugates
description: A short lesson to help you apply Antibody-Drug Conjugates.

hook.text: Chemotherapy poisons all dividing cells — what if you could deliver the poison only to cancer cells?

buildup.text: Antibody-drug conjugates link a toxic payload to an antibody — the antibody finds the tumor, the drug kills it.

discovery.text: A chemical linker holds the payload — it breaks only inside the cancer cell, releasing the poison precisely.

twist.text: Early ADCs failed because linkers broke too early — releasing toxin in the bloodstream. Stable linkers fixed this.

climax.text: Enhertu treats breast cancer with HER2 — its bystander effect kills even neighboring cancer cells that lack the target.

punchline.text: A guided missile with a warhead — ADCs deliver chemo to the doorstep.

quiz.question: How do antibody-drug conjugates reduce chemotherapy side effects?
options: They use a less toxic form of chemotherapy drug
The antibody delivers the toxic payload specifically to cancer cells, sparing healthy tissue
They prevent the drug from entering the bloodstream entirely

details.summary: Antibody-drug conjugates link a monoclonal antibody to a potent cytotoxic drug, delivering chemotherapy directly to cancer cells while sparing healthy tissue. The antibody targets specific tumor markers, acting like a guided missile for precision oncology.
details.whyItMatters: ADCs combine the targeting precision of antibodies with the killing power of chemotherapy. They represent one of the fastest-growing classes of cancer drugs, with over a dozen approved and hundreds in clinical trials.
takeaways: ADCs deliver toxic drugs directly to cancer cells via antibody targeting
The linker chemistry determines drug stability and release timing
Over a dozen ADCs are FDA-approved with many more in development

faq.question: How does an antibody-drug conjugate find cancer cells?
faq.answer: The antibody component recognizes a specific protein overexpressed on cancer cell surfaces but not healthy cells. After binding, the entire ADC is internalized by the cancer cell, where the linker breaks and releases the cytotoxic drug to kill the cell from within.

faq.question: What advantages do ADCs have over traditional chemotherapy?
faq.answer: ADCs can use drugs too toxic for conventional chemotherapy because they deliver them selectively to cancer cells. This reduces systemic side effects like hair loss and nausea while increasing tumor drug concentration by up to 100-fold compared to untargeted chemotherapy.
